my husband and i moved from Massachusetts to California a few years ago, just because. We were 34 (me) and 30 (him) years old at the time. it was a little scary at first but now has worked out pretty wonderfully - i do miss my family like crazy, though.

advice?

  1. scrape together some savings before you go. we didn't have much (a few thousand i think?), but we had a small cushion anyway, and it was really crucial. suck it up and don't buy the things you "want" now in favor of saving for the future move. it took about a month to find my first job out here, and then when that turned out to be a total disaster, about another month after i quit to find the second job. i am a nurse with a bachelors degree and 10 years of experience - i did NOT expect to have difficulty finding work. my point is - you never really know how it will pan out so having a little bit of savings will help keep your stress level more manageable.

  2. stay open-minded. you might not end up in the town or city you want, or in the kind of job you thought you wanted, but the adventure will be a worthwhile one no matter what. you might find that the things you thought were important to you turn out to not be so important after all, and that's okay too.

  3. be careful about staying with friends. i've never done it myself, but i have watched way too many people ruin their friendships with each other either by offering a place to stay or overstaying their welcome. that doesn't mean you shouldn't do it...just be mindful.

  4. finally: be nervous. wonder if you're making a mistake. and then take a deep breath and let that shit go.

happy adventuring! :)

short version: Have i? Yes. How'd it go? Not perfect, but good. Advice? Too much. :)
longer version:

Back in early '99 (in my late 20s), I was in a situation where my contract job was coming to an end and the company had just instituted new rules for contractors that would have forced long breaks between contracts. Additionally, my apartment lease was ending at almost the same time and, like you, I had a friend in another part of the country that promised sofa space and a "good adventure".

So I dumped most of my worldly goods into a storage unit, packed the bare essentials in my car and went cross-country for what I thought would be at least 3 or 4 weeks, but might last as long as a few months. I ended up staying there for about a year and a half. While it wasn't all smooth sailing, I made a lot of new friends and ultimately (after a few other moves) ended up spending an additional ~7 years there, and, if I get this new job, I'll be moving back there again for at least another few years.

It will be challenging, and can be quite expensive, but having at least one supportive friend there to help you "land" makes a HUGE difference. Make sure your friend knows - consistently - how much you appreciate them and that you don't "take advantage" of them. It one thing to say that they're willing to put you up "as long as needed" - it's another to be still there four or five months in.

I could ramble for pages and pages with various bits of relocation advice - but I imagine that the differences in our situations would make some/much of it moot. Are there any specific issues you're concerned about? Anything specific I/we might be able to help answer?

Cashmere currently has 72 different variables which control the colours of various elements (36 for each of day and night mode). You can find these variables either in '_settings.scss' or at the beginning of 'cashmere.cat.scss'.

For example, this is the variable that sets the background of the header: $header-background: hsl(205, 50%, 40%);

And here's where it shows up in '_header.scss':

#header {
 position: fixed;
 width: 100%;
 height: 66px;
 background: $header-background;
}

For any of these settings, you can use any valid CSS color. I have a lot of HSL colours because I find them easier to visualize, but you can declare the colour any way you like: hex, RGBa, etc..

 

The other type of value in the colour settings are Sass functions. Here's an example of that:

$thumbnail-background: darken($body-background, 25%);

This takes the body background we've already defined, darkens it by 25%, and uses that for the thumbnail background. We could set the variable $thumbnail-background to anything -- it doesn't have to be a function -- but it makes it easier to work with because you don't need to change all 72 variables. If you changed the body background to red, the thumbnail would become a dark red.

Here are some other basic available functions and here's the full list. Sass will even mix two colours together if you want.

 

It's also possible to use another variable without a function. Take this example:

$text-color: #111;
[...]
$sidebar-text-color: $text-color;

The sidebar text can be made a different colour from the other text, but by default they are the same. If you change $text-color to #000, you don't need to remember to also change $sidebar-text-color. Note that the variable must always be defined higher up in the document before it can be used. Sass would give us an error if we tried to do this:

$variable-A: $variable-B;
$variable-B: #fff;
A short guide to colour settings in Cashmere.
